lessons.symptom: A previously green PR becomes non-mergeable or main moves through overlapping control-plane changes.
lessons.rootCause: High repository churn invalidates stale base assumptions.
lessons.failedApproach: Force-merging or continuing to reason from the old base.
lessons.requiredAction: Re-read current main, check changed-path and contract overlap, and rebuild only the proven delta from fresh main when overlap exists.
lessons.prevention: Always run the current-main conflict/contract gate immediately before expected-head merge.
lessons.evidenceRule: A candidate is mergeable only when its exact head is green and current-main conflict evidence is fresh.

lessons.symptom: A log or workflow result appears relevant but belongs to an older candidate or earlier RED run.
lessons.rootCause: Evidence was selected by workflow name or chronology instead of exact SHA/run identity.
lessons.failedApproach: Treating an old green or red log as proof for the current candidate.
lessons.requiredAction: Bind every claim to exact candidate SHA, run id, job id and artifact where applicable.
lessons.prevention: Reject evidence whose head_sha does not equal the candidate being evaluated.
lessons.evidenceRule: No success or failure claim may use a run from another SHA.

lessons.symptom: A semantic SQL regression test counts tokens in comments and reports an extra auth.uid or forbidden pattern.
lessons.rootCause: Raw-text regex assertions included SQL comments.
lessons.failedApproach: Changing correct migration semantics to satisfy a comment-sensitive regex.
lessons.requiredAction: Strip SQL comments before semantic regex/count assertions.
lessons.prevention: Semantic SQL tests operate on normalized executable SQL, not comments.
lessons.evidenceRule: A test failure is actionable only after proving the matched token occurs in executable SQL.

lessons.symptom: A later security migration accidentally restores privileges revoked by an earlier migration.
lessons.rootCause: Tests inspected migrations independently instead of evaluating final effective grants.
lessons.failedApproach: Declaring least privilege from one migration file in isolation.
lessons.requiredAction: Test final cross-migration access contracts and verify live effective privileges.
lessons.prevention: Maintain repo-wide cross-migration grant regression tests for protected views/tables.
lessons.evidenceRule: Security state is the final effective database state, not intent in an individual migration.

lessons.symptom: Advisor reports unindexed foreign keys or unused indexes on small/new tables.
lessons.rootCause: Static lint information lacks workload, growth and latency context.
lessons.failedApproach: Creating or dropping indexes solely to make INFO findings disappear.
lessons.requiredAction: Observe table size, query frequency, FK delete/update behavior and latency; require repeated qualifying evidence before candidate DDL.
lessons.prevention: INFO remains OBSERVE until evidence thresholds are met; post-change outcome must be remeasured.
lessons.evidenceRule: Performance DDL requires measured net benefit, not a clean advisor screen.

lessons.symptom: UPDATE/DELETE triggers protect append-only rows while service_role still has TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER privileges.
lessons.rootCause: Trigger-based immutability does not prevent TRUNCATE and broad table privileges survived default grants.
lessons.failedApproach: Assuming immutable UPDATE/DELETE triggers alone make a ledger append-only.
lessons.requiredAction: REVOKE ALL and explicitly GRANT only SELECT, INSERT for the runtime role; verify effective live privileges.
lessons.prevention: Append-only ledgers require both immutable triggers and an explicit least-privilege grant allowlist.
lessons.evidenceRule: TRUNCATE, UPDATE, DELETE, REFERENCES and TRIGGER must all be false for runtime roles.

lessons.symptom: service_role retains capabilities not required by the application runtime.
lessons.rootCause: Broad inherited/default grants were not replaced with an explicit allowlist.
lessons.failedApproach: Revoking only the privileges that happened to be noticed.
lessons.requiredAction: Use REVOKE ALL followed by the smallest explicit GRANT set and verify with has_table_privilege.
lessons.prevention: Every server-only store has a declared runtime privilege allowlist.
lessons.evidenceRule: Live privilege probes, not migration text, determine GREEN.

lessons.symptom: A required external setting cannot be changed through the connected tool.
lessons.rootCause: The available connector exposes read/advisor/database actions but not the required configuration mutation.
lessons.failedApproach: Claiming completion, inventing a mutation, or substituting an unrelated change.
lessons.requiredAction: Keep the obligation open as BLOCKED_HARD_BOUNDARY or pending authorized capability and continue all independent safe work.
lessons.prevention: Discover connector capability before promising external configuration mutation.
lessons.evidenceRule: Absence of a supported mutation action can never be counted as successful configuration.

lessons.symptom: Netlify reports ready while production may still point at a previous commit.
lessons.rootCause: Deploy health and source identity are separate properties.
lessons.failedApproach: Treating state=ready as proof that current GitHub main is deployed.
lessons.requiredAction: Compare production deploy commit_ref with fresh GitHub main SHA and require equality.
lessons.prevention: Production verification always includes exact-SHA parity plus runtime/deploy health.
lessons.evidenceRule: GREEN production requires ready AND commit_ref == canonical production SHA.

lessons.symptom: GitHub main advances but Netlify production remains on the previous SHA.
lessons.rootCause: The site deploy source is API-driven, so Git pushes do not necessarily initiate deployment.
lessons.failedApproach: Waiting indefinitely for a Git auto-deploy that is not the active delivery mechanism.
lessons.requiredAction: Inspect deploy_source and use the governed production controller/reconciliation path.
lessons.prevention: Delivery logic distinguishes Git-connected auto-deploy from API-controlled promotion.
lessons.evidenceRule: A main merge is not a deploy event unless the configured delivery mechanism proves it.

lessons.symptom: Creating a supposedly missing file returns 422 because another agent committed it concurrently.
lessons.rootCause: Concurrent agents changed branch state after the last read.
lessons.failedApproach: Blindly retrying create/update and overwriting parallel work.
lessons.requiredAction: Re-read branch head and file contents, compare semantics, then reuse or apply only the missing delta.
lessons.prevention: Treat unexpected 409/422 content writes as concurrency signals requiring refresh.
lessons.evidenceRule: No overwrite is allowed until the current remote blob is inspected.

lessons.symptom: An operational trigger needs proof but no genuine business change is pending.
lessons.rootCause: Pressure to obtain evidence can tempt creation of fake/no-op migrations or production changes.
lessons.failedApproach: Polluting production history solely to make a canary fire.
lessons.requiredAction: Use read-only/rollback-only canaries or wait for the next genuine triggering change while keeping the obligation visibly awaiting evidence.
lessons.prevention: Verification fixtures must be marked verification_only and blocked from production promotion.
lessons.evidenceRule: Production evidence must originate from a genuine governed event or a non-persistent safe probe.

lessons.symptom: A new tools/* runtime module fails the BRAIN plan before its tests can execute.
lessons.rootCause: The delivery classifier does not recognize the new subsystem path.
lessons.failedApproach: Adding one-off exceptions for each file or bypassing the fail-closed classifier.
lessons.requiredAction: Add the narrow reusable subsystem prefix plus a regression test while preserving unknown-path fail-closed behavior.
lessons.prevention: New agent/runtime families include classifier onboarding in their first contract.
lessons.evidenceRule: A new component is not production-ready until BRAIN membership is machine-proven.

lessons.symptom: An automated writer can mutate main or self-declare Published without independent production proof.
lessons.rootCause: Writer authority and production authority were not separated.
lessons.failedApproach: Allowing repository writers to write directly to main or self-merge.
lessons.requiredAction: Writers create bounded candidate PRs; independent shadow/CI/BG169 controls promotion and exact production verification.
lessons.prevention: All governed writers are candidate-only and remain pending until production evidence exists.
lessons.evidenceRule: Writer success is never sufficient production evidence.

lessons.symptom: Operational status in Notion can drift from executable repository/deployment state.
lessons.rootCause: Human projection and executable source-of-truth were treated as peers.
lessons.failedApproach: Using Notion status as authoritative proof of deployed code or workflow identity.
lessons.requiredAction: Use GitHub/BRAIN exact evidence as canonical executable truth and project validated state into Notion.
lessons.prevention: Notion receives validated projections and never independently promotes production state.
lessons.evidenceRule: Executable identity comes from exact repository/deployment evidence.

lessons.symptom: Make or agent cost rises because unchanged state is repeatedly polled and reprocessed.
lessons.rootCause: Periodic full refreshes were used where source events or deltas were available.
lessons.failedApproach: Increasing polling frequency to improve freshness.
lessons.requiredAction: Prefer event-driven triggers, cached state, delta processing and DB-local/statement-level work; keep low-frequency reconciliation as fallback.
lessons.prevention: New automations must justify polling when an event or deterministic delta trigger exists.
lessons.evidenceRule: Optimization is accepted only when cost decreases without worsening outcome freshness or reliability.

lessons.symptom: RLS policies are optimized for initplan or duplicate permissive warnings.
lessons.rootCause: Performance-oriented policy rewrites can accidentally change own-row or owner/member semantics.
lessons.failedApproach: Accepting advisor improvement without authenticated and cross-user runtime probes.
lessons.requiredAction: Pair policy optimization with exact predicate regression tests and rollback-only own-user/cross-user runtime probes.
lessons.prevention: Security semantics are protected metrics for every RLS performance change.
lessons.evidenceRule: Advisor warnings may fall only if authorized behavior is unchanged and unauthorized access remains blocked.

lessons.symptom: Database security advisor reaches zero database WARN while an Auth configuration warning remains.
lessons.rootCause: Database and Auth advisor/control planes have different scopes and mutation capabilities.
lessons.failedApproach: Reporting all security complete from a database-only clean result.
lessons.requiredAction: Report database and Auth findings separately; keep unresolved Auth controls open until independently configured and reverified.
lessons.prevention: Security completion is scoped by control plane and explicit remaining hard boundaries.
lessons.evidenceRule: Zero database WARN is not equivalent to zero platform security WARN.
